solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Time wasted in effort to make money

indicators.note: something wasted is lost or thrown away, so the time letter drops out of the effort word

parts.note: trouble is effort, as in 'took a lot of trouble'

explanation.surface: A complaint that hours squandered on hard graft are the price of earning a living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' tells you to remove T from TROUBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is the currency unit of Russia, so it is a kind of money.

clue.text: Mock one detective endlessly breaking the law

indicators.note: breaking into: the inner pieces split the law word apart

parts.note: a rule is a law
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: dick is slang for a detective

explanation.surface: A private eye is jeered at for flouting the law.
explanation.definitionFit: To ridicule is to mock or deride someone.

clue.text: Cover case in court first of all

parts.note: up means in court, as when someone is up before a judge; first of all says this piece leads
a holster is a case for a pistol

explanation.surface: A lawyer says the case must be dealt with in court before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster is to cover furniture with padding and fabric.

clue.text: Helen's mother died in open country

indicators.note: the death letter goes inside the field word

parts.note: a lea is open grassland, a meadow

explanation.surface: A woman's mother passed away out in the fields.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Leda, visited by Zeus as a swan, was the mother of Helen of Troy.

clue.text: Getting rid of heroin from shiploads caused difficulty

indicators.note: the letters that remain are troubled and thrown into a new order
taken from: the heroin letter is lifted out of the cargo word

parts.note: H is slang shorthand for heroin

explanation.surface: Customs report that removing drugs from cargoes of freight proved a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H out of SHIPLOADS, leaving SIPLOADS, which 'caused difficulty' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Disposal is the act of throwing away or dealing with something, which is what getting rid of it means.

clue.text: Runs for leader of council in one country or another

indicators.note: one thing for another means replacing it

parts.note: Iceland is a country

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone runs for council leader in one nation or another.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace the C of ICELAND, the 'leader of council', with R for 'Runs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is another country, so it stands for 'another' following 'one country'.

clue.text: Padre isn't sloshed, having imbibed last of Johnnie Walker

indicators.note: imbibed means drunk in, so the letter is taken inside
sloshed means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order
last of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A priest, who claims not to be drunk, has been at the whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnnie Walker is a whisky brand; 'Walker' is split off as the definition, and only E, the last of Johnnie, goes inside the anagram of PADREISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestrian is a person travelling on foot, that is, a walker.

clue.text: Mark abandons tense character in Corfu

indicators.note: the mark word abandons the tense letter, which leaves it

parts.note: a stigma is a mark, as of disgrace
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark drops his nerves for a role on a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character used on Corfu, a Greek island.

clue.text: Swelling initially removed by surgeon

indicators.note: the initial letter of the swelling word is taken away

parts.note: a blister is a swelling on the skin

explanation.surface: A doctor removes a lump from a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Lister was the British surgeon who pioneered antiseptic surgery.

clue.text: Excursion, for example, around wood

indicators.note: the for-example word goes around the wood

parts.note: say means for example
ash is a wood, from the ash tree

explanation.surface: A walk in the woods, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A sashay, as a noun, is a trip or outing, an excursion, mainly in American use.

clue.text: Dry out in specially heated container?

definitions.text: Dry out in specially heated container?

indicators.note: one set of letters goes inside the other
the letters of heated are specially arranged into a new order
out signals the letters of the word dry are disordered

explanation.surface: Instructions for drying something in an oven-like heated box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles the word dry, and that goes 'in' a jumble of heated signalled by 'specially'; read whole, the clue also describes the process.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove water from something, as by heating it, is to dry it out completely.

clue.text: Artist has to make pop still?

definitions.meaning: pop is a fizzy drink; to stop it fizzing is to remove its gas

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a painter needs to flatten a fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Degas is the painter's surname, and de-gas is a coined verb for removing gas from a drink.

clue.text: Instrument finally put away in brother's room

indicators.note: the final letter of the instrument word is put away, removed

parts.note: a cello is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A musician tidies his instrument into his brother's bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the last letter O from CELLO. The 'brother' is a monk.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk or friar, called brother, sleeps in a small room in a monastery known as a cell.

clue.text: Tightwad caught fish, netting a great deal

indicators.note: netting means catching inside, as fish are caught in a net

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a skate is a flat fish
a heap is a great deal, as in 'heaps of money'

explanation.surface: A miser hauls in a fish and lands a big bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightwad is a miserly person, which is a synonym for someone who will not spend.

clue.text: Promise from American woman to find weapon

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman, so from her is broad's, possessive
a word is a promise, as in giving your word

explanation.surface: An American woman promises she'll locate a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsword is a sword with a wide blade, so a weapon.

clue.text: Landed gentry disheartened about endless jury service

parts.note: lit means landed, as a bird lights on a branch

indicators.note: endless means without its ends, leaving the middle letters of jury
with its heart, all the middle letters, removed, the word keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Landowners grumble about being called up for their turn on a jury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' keeps only the outer letters of gentry; 'endless' strips both ends of jury; the first pair goes 'about' the second, after the landed word.
explanation.definitionFit: A liturgy is a form of public worship, a church service.

clue.text: Imprisonment requires you, it's said, to prepare for the outside

indicators.note: the dress word acts as the outside, wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: to dress is to prepare, as with a salad or a wound

indicators.note: it's said means the letter is chosen for how the word you sounds when spoken

parts.note: the word you, which in speech sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Being jailed means you must get ready for the world beyond the walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress can mean forcible confinement or imprisonment, an old legal sense alongside coercion.

clue.text: Heard to quote English writer in play for first time

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken as spoken, by sound

parts.note: to cite is to quote
Herbert Read, English poet and critic

explanation.surface: An actor heard quoting an English author during a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To sight-read music is to play it on first seeing it, without practice.

clue.text: She's not fair, catching animal in trap? The opposite

indicators.note: catching means one piece holds another inside it
the opposite of the surface order: the animal catches the trap

parts.note: a brute is an animal, a beast
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: Unfairly, she is caught with an animal in a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A brunette has dark hair, so she is not fair-haired.

clue.text: Daughter adds to bore's fantasies

parts.note: bore's is read as bore is; to ream is to bore out a hole, so reams = bores

explanation.surface: A daughter's daydreams are a dull bore to listen to.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreams are imaginings or wishful fancies, synonyms for fantasies.

clue.text: One fishes out dude, according to him?

definitions.text: One fishes out dude, according to him?

parts.words: One fishes out dude, according to him
parts.note: swap the initial sounds as the Oxford don famous for such slips did: fishes out dude becomes dishes out food, and one who serves food with a spoon is named for him

explanation.surface: A man explains he catches a dandy.
explanation.walkthrough: William Spooner was the Oxford don famous for swapping word-starts; his name also describes one who serves with a spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the reverend whose slips gave us spoonerisms and, playfully, one who ladles food.

clue.text: Show off, having secured grand in second bet

indicators.note: the bet holds, secures, the grand letter within it

parts.note: a wager is a bet
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A gambler boasts after winning a thousand on a second flutter.
explanation.definitionFit: To swagger is to strut or behave boastfully, which is to show off.

clue.text: Transport from south Lancashire town

parts.note: Leigh is a town in Greater Manchester, historically in Lancashire, an English county

explanation.surface: Getting a lift from a town in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleigh is a sledge drawn by horses or reindeer, a form of transport.

clue.text: Steals and completes transaction with credit card

definitions.meaning: runs a card through a reader to pay

explanation.surface: A thief buys goods using a stolen card.
explanation.definitionFit: Swipes means steals in slang and also passes a card through a reader to pay.

clue.text: Articulate writer meets another touring Oklahoma

parts.note: H. G. Wells, the English novelist

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: another writer, here a pen, the writing implement
OK is the US postal abbreviation for Oklahoma

explanation.surface: An eloquent author meets a fellow novelist on a tour of the American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone articulate speaks clearly and fluently, which describes a refined speaker.

clue.text: Climber needs a spike to ascend

indicators.note: in a down clue ascending means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: a nail is a spike

explanation.surface: A mountaineer needs a piton to get up the cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody climbing vine of tropical forests.

clue.text: Confuse with detailed check

indicators.note: de-tailed: the last letter, the tail, is cut off

parts.note: to stunt is to check, as in checking growth

explanation.surface: A detailed inspection only bewilders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'thorough' but means lose the tail: STUNT loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to daze or bewilder, which is close to confusing someone.

clue.text: In April Liberals overturned parliamentary proposal

indicators.note: in a down clue overturned means read from the bottom up, reversed
the letters lie within the run of the words April Liberals

explanation.surface: In spring the Liberal party rejected a motion in parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a draft law put before parliament for debate.

clue.text: Foremost among philosophers, having revolutionised a lot

definitions.text: Foremost among philosophers, having revolutionised a lot

indicators.note: foremost among picks the first letter of the following word
revolutionised means turned over and rearranged, so the letters of a lot are mixed up

explanation.surface: Praise for a leading thinker who changed thought enormously.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato, the ancient Greek, is among the most influential philosophers of all, and he transformed Western thought.

clue.text: Elgin losing marbles? Fellow must be sloppy

indicators.note: losing one's marbles means going mad, so the letters of Elgin go crazy

parts.note: a gent is a fellow, a man

explanation.surface: The Elgin Marbles, Greek sculptures held in the British Museum, being lost would show someone was careless.
explanation.walkthrough: The Elgin Marbles are the Parthenon sculptures in the British Museum; 'losing marbles' here just scrambles ELGIN into NEGLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent means careless or lax, a synonym for sloppy.

clue.text: Flying colours in Ordinary Level?

definitions.meaning: a flag or banner flown aloft
ordinary means normal and level means grade, so a normal grade or benchmark

explanation.surface: Passing an O level with top marks.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes O Level, the old British school exam at sixteen, and passing with flying colours; neither phrase means what it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag carried aloft, and also the normal level or benchmark of quality.

clue.text: Plight of Poland followed with keenness

parts.note: PL is the international vehicle code for Poland
edge means keenness, as the sharpness of a blade

explanation.surface: The sorry state of Poland was followed eagerly by observers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plight' looks like a predicament, but here it is the old word for a promise, as in plighting one's troth.
explanation.definitionFit: A plight in its old sense is a solemn promise or vow, just as in plighting one's troth at a wedding.
